the-hunter-relayer-evidence-submitter-an.text: The hunter: relayer, evidence submitter, and paid maintainer.

A hunter is an off-chain service that watches KERI and Cardano and lands the transactions that keep an identity's checkpoint current. It is a role any party may perform, not a trusted oracle or an identity administrator. In KERI's vocabulary it is a watcher that also submits. Earlier pages called this role the super watcher; the accepted design gives it a wage and a name.

The cross-plane problem, the evidence rules for advance, and what the role is not are those of the earlier deployed design (version 1) — its advance transactions settled on preprod. The hunter's economics (the premium paid for landing a rotation, the freeze, the conviction payout) are the accepted design, proved in the Lean and playable in the checkpoint simulator. No hunter daemon is shipped; it is epic #325.

the-cross-plane-problem.text: KERI events happen off chain. Cardano checkpoints move only when a transaction reveals and validates an event. Therefore either side can temporarily be ahead:
KERI may have a new witnessed rotation while Cardano still shows the old key state.
Cardano may have settled an advance while a particular off-chain client has not refreshed its KEL or ledger view.

The hunter observes both and closes that gap. The owner does not: the owner rotates with kli; on Cardano the controller books the registration, funds the pool and, when needed, authorizes a deposit with the new keys or a poison with the current key quorum. That asymmetry is deliberate.
The hunter seeds its own watcher from the witness OOBIs published on the endpoint board, so discovery itself does not require asking anybody.

what-a-hunter-could-do-in-version-1.text: What a hunter could do in version 1.
Against the version 1 programs published on preprod, a hunter could:
relay a public inception through premint and register;
relay a genuine witnessed rotation through advance;
monitor transaction settlement and the new unspent checkpoint.
There was no payment for any of it. Routine event relay had no on-chain fee, so a commercial relayer needed an off-chain payment model. That is the gap the accepted design closes.

the-hunters-wage-accepted-design.text: The owner keeps three separate sums in the checkpoint, and only two of them go to a payee that a hunter names:
The loop. The hunter sees the owner's rotation on KERI. It looks at Cardano:
if the pool covers the premium, it lands the rotation and names the payee of P;

if the pool is short and the checkpoint is neither frozen nor poisoned, it can freeze the checkpoint on its old keys with the same evidence. The freeze sets only the frozen bit in the datum and pays B to the payee it names. The checkpoint stays frozen until a depositing rotation restores the bond. A rotation with a short pool still lands, unpaid.
The freeze is therefore not a punishment for lag. It is what makes a non-paying owner come back, and it is bounded by two things the owner controls: fund the pool, or do not rotate.

Two hunters racing produce one winner. If the pool covers P the first advance wins and the second fails on the spent input; if it does not, the first freeze pays B and the second is refused because the checkpoint is already frozen.

No bounty. There is no payment for detecting misbehaviour, because a flow whose profitability depends on another party's misbehaviour invites staged misbehaviour. The single exception is the conviction, and it is an exception on principled ground: two rotations of different content at one sequence, both valid against the same previous commitments and each receipted by its own witnesses, are a KERI verdict (duplicity), not a judgement the chain invents.

what-a-hunter-is-not.text: a service capable of rolling back settled Cardano actions.

It can submit only evidence the validators accept. When cryptographic evidence is absent, it may alert users but cannot manufacture an on-chain truth. It cannot forge controller signatures or witness receipts, activate uncommitted keys, move the refund address, or reset the owner's juvenility (the age her checkpoint must reach before a consumer trusts it) window: no step changes the refund address, and a deposit is signed by the keys of the epoch the rotation opens.

advance.text: the exact next KERI rotation bytes;

The advance observer reconstructs and validates the transition. The hunter cannot choose alternate keys, and the sequence number only ever moves forward — the checkpoint cannot roll back (ruling D-022).

For a rotation that cuts or adds witnesses, the version 1 validator counted receipts against the new witness set and the new toad. Whether keripy applies the same rule, or tallies against the parent's set, is not yet established. Epic #320 builds the parity oracle that settles it. It matters most on exactly the rotations that matter: witness replacement after a compromise.

freeze-accepted-design.text: The hunter presents the same evidence it would use to advance: a later witnessed rotation with its receipts. The freeze runs the advance predicate and differs only in effect. It additionally requires that the pool is below P and that the checkpoint is neither frozen nor poisoned (one locked by the owner's own declaration, which is already unconsumable); B goes to the payee the freeze names.

poison-relay-accepted-design.text: The poison is a declaration the owner's current key quorum authorizes; the model does not yet specify the bytes they sign, and no validator implements the poison spend. It is never witnessed, and anyone may land it. A hunter that carries poisons promptly is doing the most valuable thing in the system: the poison's whole purpose is to be fast.

convict-accepted-design.text: The conviction proof is narrower than any lag evidence. It requires a rival rotation at the native sequence of the accepted one, valid against the same previous commitments: it satisfies the previous next-key commitment and its own signing threshold, carries receipts from its own derived witnesses, and differs in complete content from the accepted one. The comparison runs against the authenticated context the checkpoint selects, never one the rival chooses.

A stranger cannot manufacture this. Only a holder of the pre-committed keys could have signed the second rotation, and each rotation needs the receipts of its own derived witnesses at its own threshold; the comparison does not itself require the two receipt sets to overlap. The conviction reveals a commitment opened beforehand, within its window and naming this identifier, deployment and key state; its payee takes D_reg in full, and the freeze bond still held and the pool go to the refund address. The checkpoint becomes a pending termination; the booking that moves the pending output into the termination request and the fold that consumes that request then retire the identity, which is terminal.

operational-loop.text: maintain verified KEL state for watched AIDs, seeded from the endpoint board;
resolve each AID's current Cardano checkpoint and read its pool;
compare the native KERI sequence with the checkpoint's;

choose the permitted public projection — a rotation (paid when the pool covers P, unpaid otherwise), a freeze when the pool is below P and the checkpoint is clean and unfrozen, a poison relay when one exists, a conviction when the proof is in hand and its commitment is eligible, and no transaction when evidence is incomplete;
construct the transaction for the chosen step with the evidence it needs;
evaluate and budget every script purpose;
record transaction IDs and evidence provenance.
The service must never treat mempool acceptance as settlement.

freshness-and-availability.text: A hunter improves discovery latency but cannot eliminate KERI witness outages, network partitions, Cardano inclusion delay, chain rollbacks, block-level censorship, or a colluding witness threshold.

Applications should not silently outsource all freshness policy to one hunter. A relying application checks a checkpoint’s age against the juvenility window W. It can use a clean, unfrozen checkpoint only once the current slot reaches its birth slot plus W. The planned devnet measurement of the time from witness receipt to landed rotation will inform the choice of W in epic #325.

credential-plane-extension.text: Later, a hunter may also follow ACDC credential chains and TEL revocation events. That duty is separate from identity checkpoint authority: identity relay answers which keys currently control the AID; credential monitoring answers which issued roles remain valid. Only the first plane is in M1.

security-principle.text: The hunter is safe to make permissionless because it pays to submit public proofs whose key state is fixed by the evidence, and nothing in the validators pays the submitter as such: the rest of the outcome is fixed by the whole transaction, which names the payee and the deposit option; when the pool covers the premium, the premium goes from value the owner chose to keep there to the address the rotation names, which need not be the submitter's; a rotation with a short pool lands unpaid. A hostile hunter can withhold its own service or waste fees on invalid transactions. It cannot install a key state other than the one its evidence establishes, take D_reg without an accepted conviction, or take B while the pool pays. For a paid rotation the submitter names the payee of the premium from the pool; a freeze pays the bond to the address it names. When the owner's new keys have signed a deposit intent, the same evidence supports a rotation that keeps the frozen state and one that deposits and clears it; the intent authorizes the deposit amount for that checkpoint input.
